{{Short description|Argentine theoretical physicist (1930–2022)}}
'''Alberto Sirlin''' (born 25 November 1930, in [[Buenos Aires]], died February 23, 2022, in [[New York City]]) was an Argentine theoretical physicist, specializing in [[particle physics]].<ref>{{cite journal|author=Porrati, Massimo|authorlink=Massimo Porrati|title=Alberto Sirlin|journal=Journal of Physics G: Nuclear and Particle Physics|volume=29|issue=1|year=2003|doi=10.1088/0954-3899/29/1/003}}</ref>

==Biography==
Sirlin studied from 1948 to 1952 at the University of Buenos Aires, where he received his doctorate in 1953 under the supervision of [[Richard Gans]]. In 1953–1954 Sirlin was a fellow at the [[Centro Brasileiro de Pesquisas Físicas]] in Rio de Janeiro, where he took several graduate courses, including one taught by [[Richard Feynman]].<ref>{{cite arXiv|author=Sirlin, Alberto|authorlink=Alberto Sirlin|title=Remembering a Great Teacher|year=2015|eprint=1512.08247|class=physics.hist-ph}}</ref> Sirlin was in 1954–1955 at the University of California at Los Angeles (UCLA) and in 1955–1957 at the [[Cornell University]], where in 1958 he received a doctorate under the supervision of [[Toichiro Kinoshita|Tōichirō Kinoshita]]. From 1957 to 1959 he was a research assistant at Columbia University. At [[New York University]] he was from 1959 to 1961 an assistant professor, from 1961 to 1968 an associate professor, and from 1968 a full professor, retiring in 2008.<ref name=APS>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?first_nm=Alberto&last_nm=Sirlin&year=2002|title=2002 J.J. Sakurai Prize for Theoretical Particle Physics, AlbertoSirlin|website=American Physical Society}}</ref><ref name=IAS>{{cite web|title=Alberto Sirlin|website=Institute for Advanced Study|date=9 December 2019|url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/alberto-sirlin}}</ref>

Sirlin did research in the 1950s on radiative corrections in the theory of muon decay, i.e. higher-order corrections in the allowed weak interactions of [[quantum electrodynamics]] (QED).<ref>{{cite journal|author=Behrends, Ralph E.|author2=Finkelstein, Robert|authorlink2=Finkelstein|author3=Sirlin, A.|title=Radiative corrections to decay processes|journal=Physical Review|volume=106|issue=2|year=1955|pages=866–873|doi=10.1103/PhysRev.101.866|bibcode=1956PhRv..101..866B}}</ref> In 1960 Sirlin and Ralph E. Behrends discovered the nonrenormalization theorem for partially conserved [[vector current]]s in the SU(2) theory of weak interactions and suggested the theorem's generalization to higher symmetry. Their theorem plays an important role in experimentally verifying predictions from the [[Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa matrix]].<ref>{{cite journal|author=Choudhury, Deo C.|author2=Feinberg, Gerald|authorlink2=Gerald Feinberg|author3=Sirlin, Alberto|title=Obituary. Ralph E. Behrends|date=1 May 1990|journal=Physics Today|volume=43|issue=5|pages=98–99|doi=10.1063/1.2810573|bibcode=1990PhT....43e..98C|doi-access=free}}</ref> Beginning in the 1970s Sirlin did research with his student [[William J. Marciano]] on higher-order corrections in leptonic decays.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Marciano, W.J.|author2=Sirlin, A.|title=Deviation from electron-muon universality in the leptonic decays of the intermediate bosons|journal=Physical Review D|year=1973|volume=8|issue=10|pages=3612–3615|doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.8.3612|bibcode=1973PhRvD...8.3612M}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Marciano, W.J.|author2=Sirlin, A.|title=Dimensional regularization of infrared divergences|journal=Nuclear Physics B|volume=88|issue=1|pages=86–98|doi=10.1016/0550-3213(75)90527-1|year=1975|bibcode=1975NuPhB..88...86M}}</ref> With [[Tsung-Dao Lee]] and [[Richard M. Friedberg]], Sirlin did research on non-topological soliton solutions in quantum field theory.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Friedberg, R.|author2=Lee, T.D.|author3=Sirlin, A.|title=Class of scalar-field soliton solutions in three space dimensions|journal=Physical Review D|volume=13|issue=10|year=1976|pages=2739–2761|doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.13.2739|bibcode=1976PhRvD..13.2739F}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Friedberg, R.|author2=Lee, T. D.|author3=Sirlin, A.|title=Gauge-field non-topological solitons in three space-dimensions (I)|journal=Nuclear Physics B|volume=115|issue=1|year=1976|pages=1–31|doi=10.1016/0550-3213(76)90274-1|bibcode=1976NuPhB.115....1F}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Friedberg, R.|author2=Lee, T. D.|author3=Sirlin, A.|title=Gauge-field non-topological solitons in three space-dimensions (II)|journal=Nuclear Physics B|volume=115|issue=1|year=1976|pages=32–47|doi=10.1016/0550-3213(76)90275-3|bibcode=1976NuPhB.115...32F}}</ref>

Sirlin was elected a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 1971.<ref name=IAS/> He was in the academic year 1983–1984 a [[Guggenheim Fellow]] and in 1997 received the [[Alexander von Humboldt Award]]. In 2002 Sirlin and William J. Marciano received the [[Sakurai Prize]] for their collaborative research on the theory of [[electroweak]] interactions.<ref name=APS/>
